title: Two for Two: Kaushal Repeats in Buckaroo Bowl II as Ramon Crashes the Party and Sonny Repeats Too
dek: Habibsters went 11-3 and won a second straight title by 116 points, a 7-7 Araleasers team made a run nobody saw coming, and Ben Dover finished last for the second year in a row.
body: The 2024 season was supposed to answer one question: could anyone take the belt from Kaushal? Fourteen weeks, three playoff games and zero trades later, the answer was a firm no. Habibsters went 11-3, earned the top seed again, and won Buckaroo Bowl II by a margin so large it should have come with a mercy rule. Two Bowls, two trophies, one manager.

The season opened with a warning shot from an unlikely place. Ramon's Araleasers dropped 166.58 in Week 1, the highest single-week score of the year and a full 10 points better than the league's best week in 2023. It did not launch a juggernaut. Araleasers wobbled to 7-7 with 1,430.9 points, fourth in the league, and settled into the third seed. But anyone who remembered that opening Sunday knew the ceiling was in there somewhere.

The regular season's strangest story belonged to Randy. The fumblers scored 1,595.1 points, the most in the league and more than 70 ahead of the champion, and turned that into an 8-6 record and the second seed. Alan's Team Pillbert was a similar puzzle in a different key: third in points at 1,473.9, yet 6-8, and still in the playoffs as the fourth seed. Meanwhile, nobody in the league made a single trade for the second straight year. Six managers, fourteen weeks, and every roster move handled strictly in-house, which is either six people with total confidence in their drafts or six people who could not agree on anything.

The semifinals went one-for-two on chalk. Habibsters handled Team Pillbert 296.96 to 245.08 over two weeks, a 51.88-point cushion that let Habib cruise into another title game. The other side was the upset of the year. The league's top-scoring offense picked the worst possible moment to go quiet, and The fumblers managed just 176.14 over the two weeks while Araleasers posted 202.44 to win by 26.30. Randy, who led everyone in points, was out, and Ramon, who spent the season at .500, was in the Bowl.

Buckaroo Bowl II never had a second act. Habibsters scored 261.44 over the two weeks, Araleasers managed 145.28, and the 116.16-point margin nearly doubled Kaushal's winning margin from Bowl I. Ramon's Cinderella run deserved a better ending, and a runner-up finish from a 7-7 team is nothing to be ashamed of, but the clock struck midnight the moment the opponent was the defending champ. Alan took third and Randy fourth, a quiet finish for the man whose team had the loudest stat sheet.

Down at the bottom, the consolation ladder sorted out two 5-9 teams. Mekhi's Dawgs scored 1,413.5 points and climbed to fifth, while Sonny's Ben Dover finished last for the second straight season. The numbers made the case before the ladder did: Ben Dover scored 1,304.3 points, more than 109 behind anyone else, and owned the lowest single week of the year with 44.1 in Week 12, a score that would barely have qualified as a good half for the champs. Sonny's worst-to-first story would eventually arrive, but in 2024 it was still firmly in the worst chapter.

So the second page of the history book looks a lot like the first. Kaushal on top, Ben Dover on the bottom, no trades in between, and a growing sense that the rest of the league was going to need a new plan. The 2024 season did add some fresh plot lines: Randy proving points and wins are not the same thing, Alan sneaking into the playoffs under .500, and Ramon reminding everyone that a 7-7 team with a 166-point week in its back pocket is dangerous in December. Buckaroo Bowl II belongs to the Habibsters, and the dynasty talk is officially no longer a joke.
